items.stem: Which chart best shows a trend in a single metric over time?

options.rationale: Correct: line charts are designed to show change over a continuous axis such as time.
Pie charts show parts of a whole, not trends over time.
A single value cannot show a trend.
Scatter of categories does not convey a time trend.

items.explanation: Correct: line charts are designed to show change over a continuous axis such as time.

items.stem: Which choices make a chart more accessible and honest? (Select TWO)

options.text: Using a colour-blind-safe palette rather than red/green alone
options.rationale: Correct: colour-blind-safe palettes keep categories distinguishable.

options.text: Starting a bar chart's value axis at zero
options.rationale: Correct: a zero baseline prevents exaggerating differences.

options.text: Truncating the axis to make small differences look large
options.rationale: That misleads the reader and is dishonest.

options.text: Encoding categories only by red vs green
options.rationale: Red/green alone fails for many colour-blind readers.

items.explanation: Correct: colour-blind-safe palettes keep categories distinguishable.; Correct: a zero baseline prevents exaggerating differences.

items.stem: In Matplotlib, why prefer the object-oriented (Figure/Axes) API for complex figures?

options.text: It gives explicit control over each axes object and scales to multi-panel layouts
options.rationale: Correct: explicit Figure/Axes handles make complex, multi-panel figures predictable.

options.text: It is the only way to draw a line
options.rationale: Lines can be drawn either way; this is about control.

options.text: It automatically chooses the chart type for you
options.rationale: It does not auto-select chart types.

options.text: It disables the pyplot module entirely
options.rationale: pyplot still exists; the APIs coexist.

items.explanation: Correct: explicit Figure/Axes handles make complex, multi-panel figures predictable.
